title: Jake's Oyster Stew
tagline: Oysters, butter, milk. Edges curl, then it's done.
description: Jake's oyster stew from a typed family card: a pint of shucked oysters cooked gently in butter with a little flour, Worcestershire and salt, then finished with two quarts of milk and celery salt. About 20 minutes, served hot.
ingredients: 1 pint shucked oysters, drained and washed
steps: In a soup kettle, blend the flour, salt, Worcestershire and 4 Tbsp water into a smooth paste.
Add the oysters and butter. Simmer over very low heat 3-4 minutes, stirring gently, until the edges of the oysters curl.
Add the milk and heat, stirring, until steaming hot. Keep it below a boil.
Add celery salt to taste. Serve hot.
notes: Curled edges are the doneness signal. Past that, oysters go rubbery fast, so get the milk in right away.
Don't let the milk boil. It can scorch on the bottom or break, and the oysters toughen.
The card drains and washes the oysters. If you want a stronger oyster flavor, strain the liquor and add it with the milk.
3 tsp salt is the card's amount for 2 quarts of milk. Start with 2 and taste before the celery salt goes in if your butter is salted.
troubleshooting: Rubbery oysters → cooked too long before the milk; pull at the first curl.
Grainy or split stew → milk boiled; keep it at a steam, not a bubble.
Lumps of flour → paste not smooth before the oysters went in; whisk the flour and water first.
